value.rationale: The embedded difference is the quantity a controller uses to decide whether a step is accurate, so a nonzero root with nonzero true defect is a natural reliability invariant. The classical Fehlberg pair has such a root on the simplest scalar test equation, with a \(4.21\%\) one-step relative miss, unbounded true-error-to-estimator ratio near the root, and an exact fixed-step or maximum-step-clamped trajectory whose estimator is always zero while global relative error tends to one. This supplies a compact stress test and a structural warning for controller safeguards.
